Riley, I've graded submission s2 and written the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. You got 3 of 6 right, 2 partly right and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes it an agent. |
| q2 | Correct | The model outputs a request, and the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | Wrong | You picked "let it run longer". All 40 steps were already in context with the same failing result, so more steps add nothing. A step limit that stops the loop and reports back is the safeguard. |
| q4 | Partial | Your count of 4 is right, but you wrote that the model runs the tools itself. In q2 you said the model only outputs a request, so who executes it? |
| q5 | Correct | The result goes back in as the next input, and the model uses it to pick its next step. |
| q6 | Partial | The name helps, but the model also gets a description of each tool. If the model has never seen the tool's code, what other text could it be given? |

**One thing to work on:** the model only reads text and requests actions, and the program does everything else.

**Next step:** write the loop for "Is the laser cutter free tomorrow?" as numbered lines, each marked "model" or "program". Then mark the line where a step limit would stop it.

The reviewer asked for a "Try first:" question on the correct and wrong items too. The grader declined, because its rules allow one only on partial items. I couldn't read the answer key myself, so I couldn't check that. The review ran the two passes allowed. No verdicts changed. The review record is in `review-records/0001-s2-grade.md`.

I also added learning record `0003-model-requests-program-runs-tools.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. Submission s1 is still ungraded, and you can ask me to grade it if you want that.
